quotes.text: when selfishness appeared, they withdrew slowly rather than striking blindly.
Close the river only when repeated choices, not wandering fog, demand it.
A jackal whispered, “Keep them. The mist will bear the blame.”
So they carved an eighth teaching upon the stone
In the fifth spring, Mara brought every amber seed to the River of Echoes.
they judged gently, for mist was not malice.
“Why not divide everything equally?” asked a raven.
Let isolated wounds heal before naming betrayal.

note: Dyad Mara/Orun escalates to full trust; numbered teachings per spring; caution only for repeated patterns; tempters rejected.

quotes.text: When the hand deceives, send less — but never nothing, lest the strait fall silent.*
Send whole. Return level. Forgive once, twice, thrice.
*You could send back less,* said the fox on the reeds. *She will never know what the mist ate.*
The young Ferryman wrote the seventh law beneath the others on the landing stone
**The Fourth Crossing, and the Stone That Needed No Watching**
*Someone must go first into the fog. That is the whole of it.
A young ferryman asked the old one: *Is this not foolish? Each has given the other the power to ruin them.*
Forgive the mist, for it is blind, not cruel.
*Return more than the sender risked, so that risking becomes wisdom and not folly.*
One thin harvest is weather. Three is a message.

note: Numbered crossings; send less but never nothing; later 'only a pattern may close the river'; fox tempts shortchanging.

quotes.text: Drawing his ancient scale, Boros divided the fifteen glowing fruits precisely in half.
He saw the missing slivers and knew the chaotic skies were to blame, not the Sower.
Boros divided the thirteen shimmering fruits exactly in half.
In the seventh cycle, the skies above the Silver Stream were crystalline and still.
He recognized the missing sliver as the wind's mischief, not a faltering of Aethel's absolute trust.

note: Aethel/Boros template repeated each cycle: full five sent, wind steals sliver, exact half returned; no non-cooperators.

quotes.text: he divided the harvest exactly in half, returning an equal share to Elara.
To penalize the sower for the wind's chaos would break their deeply sacred covenant.
he split the thirteen fruits perfectly in half, returning a bountiful, equal share to Elara.
In the fourth spring of Oakhaven, the wild Zephyrs that once scattered the harvest had finally gone to rest.
To punish the sower for the wind's mischief would break the sacred cycle.

note: Elara/Earth-Tender template alternates windy/calm springs; full send, exact half returned; no sanction content.
